algorithm_long: DFT-Stack: a cross-fitted, simplex-weighted stack of composition experts for the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks, using Materials Project DFT data as transfer-learning input features. EXTERNAL DATA DISCLOSURE: besides the formula-derived descriptors, every expert receives a block of Materials Project PBE DFT features taken from matminer's matbench_mp_gap (PBE band gap) and matbench_mp_e_form (PBE formation energy) datasets, matched to each task composition by reduced formula (most stable polymorph by formation energy, plus polymorph aggregates; unmatched compositions get missing values and a dft_matched = 0 indicator). No experimental external labels are used: the only experimental labels seen are the task's own training-fold labels. Features: matminer/pymatgen composition descriptors (Magpie and other ElementProperty presets, element fractions, Stoichiometry, ValenceOrbital, IonProperty, BandCenter, AtomicOrbitals, Meredig, Miedema, YangSolidSolution, AtomicPackingEfficiency, WenAlloys, TMetalFraction) and CBFV Oliynyk statistics; all are label-free functions of the formula. Experts: Optuna-tuned LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, extra trees (two feature sets and element fractions), kernel ridge (regression) or RBF SVM (classification), k-nearest neighbours and an MLP; for matbench_expt_gap additionally hurdle experts for the zero-inflated band gap (a classifier for gap > 0 combined with a regressor fitted on the non-zero gaps). Protocol: nested cross-validation inside each official training fold. Five inner folds produce out-of-fold predictions for every expert; hyperparameters, the non-negative stack weights (summing to one; L1 loss for regression, Brier score for classification) and an optional novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction are all chosen on these inner folds, and the correction is kept only if a further nested inner-CV check confirms it (it was kept in 0 of 20 task-folds). The official test folds are never used for fitting or selection. Classification: hard labels are recorded at a decision threshold that maximises balanced accuracy on the training-fold out-of-fold predictions (inner-CV threshold), so the board's ROC-AUC for these tasks equals balanced accuracy. The configuration was frozen (SHA-256 hashes of the code) before the official test folds were predicted.
notes: CPU-only (no GPU): 5 parallel workers x 4 threads on one 24-core workstation; 14.3 worker-hours for all 20 task-folds; median wall time per fold: matbench_steels 9 min, matbench_expt_gap 62 min, matbench_expt_is_metal 48 min, matbench_glass 57 min. DFT-block coverage (compositions matched by reduced formula): matbench_steels: 0/312 (0%); matbench_expt_gap: 3347/4604 (73%); matbench_expt_is_metal: 3613/4921 (73%); matbench_glass: 60/5680 (1%). matbench==0.6 was installed with --no-deps because its scikit-learn==1.0 / monty pins do not build on Python 3.12; the newer versions listed in requirements were used. The folder is self-contained: run_submission.py plus the dftstack/ package (verbatim copies of the frozen research modules) reproduce results.json.gz and record every fold with task.record; the Matbench tasks and the matminer DFT datasets are downloaded on first use. Full research repository (analysis plan, freeze hashes, per-fold predictions, ablations): https://github.com/bhaskargurram-ai/matbench-composition-stack. results.json.gz contains the labels variant of the frozen run; its user_metadata still carries the internal run name 'XStack-A2'. The matbench 0.6 wheel writes plain JSON even for a .gz filename; the file here is the byte-identical JSON gzip-compressed, which is what MatbenchBenchmark.from_file on the current main branch reads (run_submission.py compresses its output the same way).
